newsitem.title: ITALY: Greenpeace stages soya protest at Nestle in Italy.
newsitem.headline: Greenpeace stages soya protest at Nestle in Italy.

text.p: Activists from the environmental group Greenpeace hung a banner across the top of a Nestle factory in Milan on Tuesday to protest against the use of genetically-altered soybeans in its products, witnesses said.

"This is a serious form of discrimination against Italian consumers who stated that they do not want to eat unnatural food, whose effects on human health are unknown," said Alessandro Gianni, a spokesman for Greenpeace Italy.
Greenpeace said in a statement it was protesting against a decision by the Italian arm of the Swiss food giant to use altered soya.
A call to Nestle Italiana SpA in Milan was not immediately returned.

Nestle SA, the world's largest food company, has insisted that genetically modified soybeans are safe and of high quality and it intended to use them in its products despite protests from environmental activists. Its German arm, however, has agreed not to use the beans.
Greenpeace activists scaled the Milan factory and hung a banner reading: "No to experiments on Italians. No to Mad Soya in Italy".
The group said the Milan protest was one of several it was staging in the "gene-bean" dispute across Europe on Tuesday.
